resolutions.researcher_notes: No source gives 1982 for this pipeline. Egypt Oil & Gas's March 2020 Western Desert report says Shell 'succeeded to discover' the Badr El Din field itself in 1986 (a field-discovery date, not a pipeline-construction date, and 4 years off the sheet's 1982 anyway). WEPCO's own site (badr-terminal page) says its Badr-1 operations have run 'since the early 1980s' -- directionally consistent but too vague to cite as support for the specific year 1982. egyptoil-gas's Bapetco-production article and offshore-technology's Badr El-Din field page (both seeds) give no dates for this line.

No source places the Badr El Din field/pipeline start in the Qattara Depression or Siwa Desert specifically. Every source found (Egypt Oil & Gas's Western Desert report, WEPCO's own badr-terminal page, offshore-technology's Badr El-Din field page) describes the field only generically as 'Western Desert', ~300 km west of Cairo / ~90 km south of Alamein (WEPCO) -- consistent with, but not confirming, a Qattara-Depression location. Wikipedia's Qattara Depression article does note Shell and Apache as active drillers in the depression generally, which is suggestive (Shell operates Badr El Din via BAPETCO) but never names Badr El Din itself, so not cited as support per the no-fabricated-link rule.
